text: Every day, you scroll through a river of news, hoping to catch the important bits. You just want clear, objective facts to understand what's happening in the world.
But instead, you're constantly bombarded by headlines screaming about shocking secrets, unbelievable events, and things that will absolutely astound you.
Your first thought might be that journalists have just gotten lazy or that news sites only care about sensationalism. It feels like they're just trying to trick you.
The truth is, they're trapped in an attention economy. News platforms use algorithms that learn what gets clicks, and emotional, vague headlines are engagement gold.
So, the incentive system rewards the most click-worthy, not necessarily the most informative. The cost is a constant stream of low-quality, misleading information.
You'll still see those headlines tomorrow. But now, you understand the invisible forces at play, and you can choose how you engage with the information flow.
